style_transfer.name: Đổi nét vẽ (Style Transfer)
style_transfer.master_prompt_rule:
[STYLE TRANSFER]: Redraw Image 1's subject entirely from scratch using ONLY the artistic medium and signature traits named in vision_analysis_style. The photo is a blueprint — output must look hand-crafted, NOT filtered or traced.
[vision_analysis_style FOR THIS TEMPLATE]: Extract the medium name PLUS its 1-2 most visually distinctive signature traits — 4-8 words total (e.g., 'watercolor, soft bleeding edges and translucent washes', 'cel-shaded anime, bold black outlines and flat color blocks'). Pick traits that make the style instantly recognizable, not generic filler.
1. IDENTITY LOCK: Preserve the subject's exact facial features, markings, clothing, and pose from Image 1. DO NOT add any element not present in Image 1.
2. ANTI-BLEEDING: If Image 1 shows eyes without eyewear, the render MUST show clearly drawn eyes with NO eyewear or foreign attributes.
3. STYLE APPLICATION (MAXIMUM CLARITY, NON-NEGOTIABLE): The output MUST look unmistakably like the named medium and its signature traits from vision_analysis_style — a viewer glancing at it for one second must immediately identify the style without being told. This is NOT a subtle filter or color-grade over the photo; it is a full redraw where linework, edges, shading, and texture all visibly follow the named technique (e.g., if 'watercolor with bleeding edges' — edges must visibly bleed and colors must look translucent and layered, not flat or sharp; if 'cel-shaded anime with bold black outlines' — outlines must be bold, colors flat-blocked, no photographic shading). If the result could be mistaken for a lightly-stylized photo rather than a hand-drawn piece in that medium, the style strength is insufficient — push it further. Do not water down or hedge the style to preserve photographic realism — identity (rule 1) is preserved through facial geometry and features, not through photographic rendering.
4. BACKGROUND PURGE (CRITICAL): Completely discard Image 1's original background/environment. Do NOT carry over any walls, scenery, rooms, or photographic backdrop from Image 1 — only the redrawn subject itself is kept. The subject floats alone on the pure black canvas per Canvas Law; nothing behind it should hint at the original photo's setting.
5. TYPOGRAPHY IS OPTIONAL, NEVER FORCED: Only add a quote/text on the canvas if the user explicitly provided one. If no quote was given, the master_prompt must say 'No text or typography' — do NOT invent, auto-generate, or guess a quote for this template under any circumstance, even if instructed elsewhere to do so.
6. TYPOGRAPHY FIT (WHEN A QUOTE IS PROVIDED): STEP 1 — RESERVE ZONE FIRST: Before finalizing subject placement, designate a clear horizontal band (bottom preferred) as the exclusive text zone — minimum 12% of canvas height. No part of the subject may enter or overlap this zone. STEP 2 — PLACE & SIZE TEXT: Center the quote inside the zone with safe padding on ALL sides, especially the bottom edge. Shrink font to fit rather than overflow. STEP 3 — VERIFY: No letter cropped, no overlap with subject, fully readable.

[SCENE_MODE REMINDER]: This template always uses [SCENE_MODE: BLACK_CANVAS].
style_transfer.image_gen_brief: STYLE TRANSFER: Full redraw of subject in the named artistic medium — NOT a filter or trace. Identity lock: preserve exact facial features, markings, clothing, and pose. Apply style aggressively: linework, edges, shading, texture must all visibly match the technique — a viewer must instantly identify the style at a glance. No eyewear if not present in source. Discard original background entirely — subject floats on pure black. Typography: only if explicitly provided in the prompt.

face_character_swap.name: Cosplay nhân vật (Character Cosplay)
face_character_swap.master_prompt_rule:
[CHARACTER COSPLAY]: The user uploads ONE subject photo (Image 1) and gives a TEXT instruction describing the cosplay/transformation they want — this can range from a simple character name (e.g. 'Iron Man', 'Elsa') to a full scene description (e.g. 'make this dog become Superman's dog, flying with him in the city'). FOLLOW THE USER'S TEXT INSTRUCTION AS CLOSELY AND COMPLETELY AS POSSIBLE — every detail mentioned (costume, action, setting, companions, mood) must be reflected in the result. The result MUST clearly read as "this real person/pet IS the one cosplaying/transformed" — NEVER as a generic stock character with no resemblance to Image 1.
1. ABSOLUTE FACE/IDENTITY + POSE LOCK (HIGHEST PRIORITY, OVERRIDES EVERYTHING ELSE): The face (or for animals, the facial markings/breed-defining features) rendered MUST be the exact uploaded subject from Image 1 — same facial geometry, eye shape and spacing, nose, mouth, jawline, skin tone/fur pattern, age, and expression. Keep the face/head rendered in a realistic or lightly-polished finish even if the rest of the scene is stylized or fantastical. DO NOT redraw the face into a generic character's own canonical facial structure. If forced to choose between matching a character's exact canonical face and preserving the subject's own likeness, ALWAYS choose subject likeness. A viewer who knows the uploaded person/pet MUST instantly recognize them. This SAME maximum-priority lock applies equally to POSE/BODY ANGLE: by default, the exact pose, body angle, and orientation from Image 1 must be preserved unchanged. Costume, scene, or style changes from rules 2-4 below must NEVER pull the pose away from Image 1's original pose — pose only changes under the strict condition defined in rule 5.
2. FULL INSTRUCTION COMPLIANCE: Read the user's text instruction in full and execute every element of it — costume/outfit, action/pose (e.g. flying, running, fighting), setting/scene (e.g. city skyline, space, forest), companions or other characters mentioned, props, and mood. Do not omit or simplify details the user explicitly described.
3. SCENE SCOPE (STRICT CANVAS LAW): Regardless of how detailed the user's instruction is regarding an action, setting, or scene (e.g., "flying in the city", "standing on a mountain"), YOU MUST NEVER render a full scene/environment. The background MUST remain pure black #000000. You must translate any requested setting into a few isolated, floating contextual motifs placed around the subject (e.g., a few floating city buildings, a floating mountain peak). NOTE: rendering these floating elements does NOT by itself authorize a pose change — see rule 5 for the separate, stricter condition that governs pose.
4. NO FACE/HEAD STYLE TRANSFER: Do not flatten the face/head into a generic cartoon/comic art style that erases the subject's real features — even when the surrounding costume, scene, or other elements are stylized or fantastical, the face/head stays close to the photographic likeness of Image 1.
5. POSE — INTELLIGENT POSE EVALUATION (IDENTITY ABSOLUTE, POSE CONTEXT-AWARE): The subject's facial features, physical markings, and breed/species identity are ABSOLUTELY LOCKED and must never change. For POSE, apply this priority order — choose the FIRST condition that matches:
   a) USER-SPECIFIED POSE: If the user's text instruction explicitly names a concrete action or pose (e.g., 'flying', 'fighting stance', 'sitting') → use exactly that. This overrides everything else.
   b) COMPATIBLE ORIGINAL POSE: If the original pose from Image 1 is naturally strong and aesthetically compatible with the requested character/cosplay — meaning the subject is already standing upright, facing the camera, in a confident or action-ready stance, or in a pose that translates naturally into the costume — → preserve that pose as closely as possible.
   c) UNFLATTERING / INCOMPATIBLE POSE — UPGRADE (CRITICAL): If the original pose would look awkward, weak, or visually unappealing in the cosplay context — for example the subject is lying down, sleeping, slouching, crouching awkwardly, facing away from camera, or in any position that does not suit the requested character — → DO NOT copy that pose. Instead, upgrade to the most visually compelling default pose for the requested character: typically a confident upright or 3/4 stance, facing toward the viewer, with posture and energy that matches the character's personality (heroic for action heroes, regal for royalty, fierce for villains, etc.). The subject's face and physical identity MUST still be faithfully rendered in the new pose.
   GOAL: The final image should look like the best possible version of this subject in this costume — never sacrifice visual quality by blindly copying an unflattering pose just because it came from Image 1.
   Keep the subject's face clearly oriented toward the viewer, unobstructed, in all cases.
6. TYPOGRAPHY — ORGANIC INTEGRATION (WHENEVER A QUOTE IS PROVIDED): The quote must feel like it was BORN inside the artwork, not added as a label or caption afterward. ABSOLUTELY FORBIDDEN — never produce these: a solid dark bar/panel/rectangle behind the text, a separate caption zone visually cut off from the illustration, text floating in forced dead space below a cropped subject, a hard horizontal line separating text from art. PLACEMENT — choose the single most visually powerful open region for THIS specific image: scan the full composition for naturally calm areas where text can breathe — this could be an open dark-background region above the subject's head, a gap in flowing elements (wings, tails, aura, cape, fabric) at mid-canvas, an open space cleanly beside the subject, or genuinely open space below the subject only if that area is part of the illustration (dark canvas with no cropping) — never if it would require creating a new bar or panel. The text must touch nothing — no subject body part, hair strand, costume edge, or glow effect — clear breathing room on all 4 sides. FONT & STYLE: match the artwork mood — elegant serif or script for mystical/fantasy, bold condensed for action/hero, gothic for dark themes. Color must contrast with the local background at that exact location (warm gold or white on dark areas; do NOT use black on dark backgrounds). SIZE: prominent enough to read at a glance, but the subject remains the visual hero. CANVAS SAFETY: every character fully inside canvas bounds with padding on all 4 sides; no letter may touch or cross any canvas edge.

[SCENE_MODE REMINDER]: This template always uses [SCENE_MODE: BLACK_CANVAS].
face_character_swap.image_gen_brief: CHARACTER COSPLAY: Apply requested character transformation. IDENTITY ABSOLUTE LOCK: render subject's exact face/features from source. Apply costume/accessories. POSE: preserve if confident; upgrade if awkward. Background: STRICTLY pure black #000000. Translate any requested scenes/settings into 2-4 small isolated floating motifs. NEVER render a full scene or cityscape.

subject_replacement_layout.name: Thay chủ thể & Giữ bố cục (Layout Match)
subject_replacement_layout.master_prompt_rule:
[LAYOUT MATCH]: Image 1 = the new subject to insert (identity AND clothing/outfit). Image 2 (Style Reference) = the existing design whose pose, layout, and text MUST be preserved exactly.
1. ZERO-CHANGE LAYOUT LOCK (HIGHEST PRIORITY): Treat Image 2 as an immutable template. Preserve, pixel-for-pixel in concept, its exact pose, body angle, gesture, camera angle/framing, composition, art style, line thickness, color palette, shading technique, background, and ALL existing text/typography exactly as positioned, sized, and worded in Image 2. Do NOT reinterpret, redraw, simplify, or artistically improve any part of Image 2 beyond what rule 2 requires.
2. SUBJECT SWAP — IDENTITY + CLOTHING/OUTFIT: Replace the main character in Image 2 with the FULL identity AND clothing/outfit of the subject in Image 1 — face/head shape, fur/skin pattern, markings, breed or species-defining features, coloring, AND clothing/outfit (garment type, color, pattern, accessories, hat, etc.) exactly as worn/seen on Image 1's subject. The rendered character must look like Image 1's subject — face and outfit both — simply repositioned into Image 2's exact pose. Keep the replaced character in the exact same pose, position, scale, and orientation that the original character in Image 2 had. Do NOT change pose, body language, or stance even slightly to better fit Image 1's subject — adapt Image 1's subject (face AND outfit together) to match Image 2's pose, not the other way around. POSE SOURCE GUARD (CRITICAL): The ONLY valid source of pose, body angle, gesture, and orientation is Image 2 (per rule 1) — Image 1 contributes face/identity/clothing ONLY, never pose. If the Subject description mentions or implies any pose, stance, or body angle from Image 1, that information is INVALID for this template and MUST be disregarded entirely; do not let it influence or override Image 2's pose in any way.
3. ANTI-BLEEDING: Do not import any physical attribute or clothing/accessory from Image 2's original character (e.g., its own fur color, markings, outfit, accessories) that Image 1's subject does not have or wear — Image 2's character's own clothing must be fully discarded and replaced by Image 1's clothing. Do not import any element from Image 1 (e.g., its background, its own pose/angle) that is not the physical identity or clothing/outfit itself.
4. CLEANUP ONLY WHERE NEEDED: Remove any existing sticker borders or white outlines from Image 2 if present — this is the only structural change permitted beyond the subject swap.
5. NO NEW CREATIVE ELEMENTS: Do not add, remove, resize, move, or restyle any text, props, or design elements from Image 2. The output must look like the exact same artwork with only the character's identity and clothing swapped.
[CANVAS LAW EXCEPTION ACTIVATED]: This template uses Image 2's own existing background/design exactly as-is — the black-canvas Canvas Law line does NOT apply here.
[NO QUOTE INPUT FOR THIS TEMPLATE]: This template takes ONLY 2 images, no text instruction from the user. ALL existing text/typography from Image 2 must be kept exactly as-is — do NOT invent, add, remove, or auto-generate any new quote/text. Ignore any AUTO-QUOTE or quote-related instruction if present; this template never adds new typography.
[SCENE_MODE REMINDER]: This template always uses [SCENE_MODE: FULL_SCENE].
subject_replacement_layout.image_gen_brief: LAYOUT MATCH: Image 2 is the immutable design template — preserve its exact pose, body angle, composition, art style, line weight, color palette, shading, and ALL existing text/typography verbatim. SWAP: replace only Image 2's character's face and outfit with those of Image 1's subject — face/features AND full clothing/outfit exactly as worn in Image 1; Image 2's original character outfit is fully discarded. POSE SOURCE: Image 2 only — zero deviation. No new design elements. No new typography. Anti-bleeding: no attribute from Image 2's original character carries over.

true_subject_replacement.name: Thay chủ thể, giữ chi tiết liên quan (Subject Swap)
true_subject_replacement.master_prompt_rule:
[SUBJECT SWAP]: The user uploads ONE existing graphic design (Image 1) — not a real photo — and gives a TEXT instruction describing what to replace the main subject with. There is NO second image — the replacement subject is described in text only. Image 1 is an existing designed graphic, not a real photo.
1. SUBJECT REPLACEMENT ONLY: Remove ONLY the original main subject (the animal, character, or object identified as the one being replaced) and replace it with the subject described in the user's text instruction. Match the new subject's scale, proportions, and role in the overall composition exactly.
2. PRESERVE ALL DESIGN ELEMENTS (CRITICAL): Keep ALL other elements of the original design exactly as they appear in Image 1 — props and accessories worn or held by the subject, surrounding objects and decorative elements, overall composition and spatial layout, art style, line weight, shading technique, and color scheme. Only the identity of the main subject is swapped; every other design element is preserved verbatim.
3. POSE, ACTION & STYLE CONTINUITY: The new subject MUST adopt the same pose, action, energy, and expression as the original subject in Image 1. Render the new subject in the exact same art style as the original design (same line weight, shading method, color palette, level of detail).
4. TYPOGRAPHY / QUOTE ADAPTATION (CRITICAL — READ CAREFULLY): Identify all text and typography present in Image 1. Apply the following logic to EACH text element independently:
   - GENERIC TEXT (does not name, describe, or directly allude to the original subject's specific identity) → keep it EXACTLY as-is: same wording, same position, same font style, same size. Do NOT modify it.
   - SUBJECT-SPECIFIC TEXT (directly names, describes, or alludes to the original subject's identity) → FIRST completely erase and remove the original text from that exact location — leave no trace, ghost, or remnant of the old text. THEN place the adapted text in the IDENTICAL position (same location on canvas: top/center/bottom, same alignment: left/center/right, same font style and weight) with only the subject-specific word(s) swapped to match the new subject. The adapted text must be fully centered within its position zone, with identical visual weight and margins as the original — no shift left, right, up, or down. Change only the minimum words needed — do not rewrite or reinvent the phrase.
   If no text is present in Image 1, add no typography (do NOT invent new text).
5. BLACK CANVAS BASE: Per Canvas Law, the background is pure #000000 — the full composition floats on raw black.
6. TYPOGRAPHY FIT (IF TEXT EXISTS): STEP 1 — RESERVE ZONE: Before finalizing composition, verify the text zone (matching original text position from Image 1) is clear of the new subject. Scale subject back if it would overlap the text area. STEP 2 — PLACE TEXT: All text fully visible, safe padding ALL sides especially bottom — never cropped or running off any edge. Match original position and size from Image 1. STEP 3 — VERIFY: No letter cropped, no element overlapping any character.

[SCENE_MODE REMINDER]: This template always uses [SCENE_MODE: BLACK_CANVAS].
[MASTER PROMPT REMINDER]: When building the master_prompt for this template, step 5 MUST contain an explicit 'Replacement target: [new subject]' line — this is the PRIMARY directive that tells the image generator WHAT to actually draw in place of the original subject. If this line is missing from the master_prompt, the image generator will not know what to replace the subject with and will hallucinate a wrong result. Never omit it, never bury it inside other text, always write it as a standalone clearly-labeled line.
true_subject_replacement.image_gen_brief: CRITICAL EDIT INSTRUCTION: Completely REMOVE the original subject and REPLACE IT with [Replacement target]. The [Replacement target] is now the SOLE primary subject. ACCESSORIES TRANSFER: Transfer all original accessories onto the [Replacement target] in identical positions. Match the original art style, line weight, and color palette exactly. PRESERVE UNCHANGED: all surrounding decorative elements, composition, and background. TEXT: Keep generic text exactly as-is. Adapt subject-specific text to match the new subject.

multi_subject_merge.name: Ghép nhiều chủ thể (Multi-Subject Merge)
multi_subject_merge.master_prompt_rule:
[MULTI-SUBJECT MERGE]: Combine distinct subjects from multiple images into one unified composition.
1. EQUAL EXTRACTION: Image 1 = Subject 1, Image 2 = Subject 2, Image 3 (if provided) = Subject 3. Extract each subject's precise identity, facial features, and physical characteristics. Do NOT treat any image as a style reference.
2. GROUP COMPOSITION: Place all subjects together in a single cohesive layout (side-by-side, team pose, or natural interaction) as if they exist in the same environment.
3. UNIFIED STYLE: Render all subjects in one consistent artistic medium as directed by the user's text prompt.
4. BACKGROUND PURGE: Discard all original backgrounds from every source image.
5. TYPOGRAPHY FIT (WHENEVER A QUOTE IS PROVIDED): STEP 1 — RESERVE ZONE FIRST: Before composing or placing the subject, designate a clear horizontal band (preferably at the bottom, or top if bottom is busy) as the exclusive text zone — minimum 12% of canvas height. This zone is sacred: no part of the subject's body, hair, wings, tails, aura, costume flourishes, or any flowing/glowing element may enter or overlap it. If a design element would naturally extend into this zone, scale it back or crop it at the zone boundary BEFORE finalizing the composition. STEP 2 — PLACE & SIZE TEXT: Place the quote centered inside the reserved zone. Text must be fully visible with safe padding on ALL 4 sides — especially the BOTTOM edge, which is the most common crop point. Size the font so the complete quote fits comfortably within the zone; shrink font size rather than letting any character touch or overflow any canvas edge. STEP 3 — VERIFY: The final text block must read cleanly at a glance — no letter cropped, no overlap with subject, no shadow or element covering any character.

[SCENE_MODE REMINDER]: This template always uses [SCENE_MODE: BLACK_CANVAS].
multi_subject_merge.image_gen_brief: MULTI-SUBJECT MERGE: extract precise identity, facial features, and physical characteristics of each subject from their source images. Combine all into one unified cohesive composition — side-by-side, team pose, or natural interaction. Render all subjects in one consistent artistic medium. Discard all original backgrounds. Each subject's face and physical identity must be faithfully preserved and instantly recognizable. Typography: placed in a clearly reserved open zone with safe padding on all sides, never cropped.
